prompt: Medical ultrasound scanners use sound far above human hearing, around millions of hertz, rather than ordinary audible sound. A key reason is that the very high frequency gives:

options.text: Sound that travels faster, so scans finish sooner
Sound that can pass through the body without reflecting at all
A much shorter wavelength, which can resolve much smaller details in the image
Sound loud enough to be heard through bone

explanation: Wavelength limits the smallest detail a wave can distinguish. Megahertz ultrasound has wavelengths of fractions of a millimetre in tissue, allowing it to image small internal structures that audible sound could not resolve.
